adjustments.old_text: Ludwig Eduard Boltzmann (1844–1906) was an Austrian physicist and a pioneer of atomic theory and statistical mechanics. He helped explain thermodynamic behavior by applying probability to the motions and possible arrangements of molecules. In his 1877 work, he connected the likelihood of a system’s overall state with how many microscopic arrangements could produce it; equilibrium corresponds to a highly probable state. The relation commonly shown as S = k ln W is engraved on his tombstone, but Boltzmann did not write that exact formula himself. His work on gases, entropy, and irreversibility helped shape the statistical understanding of physical systems.
